newsitem.title: USA: All debt seen paid off by Iowa race track, casino.
newsitem.headline: All debt seen paid off by Iowa race track, casino.

text.p: A highly successful race track and casino in Altoona, Iowa, has deposited enough money with Polk County to pay off all the outstanding debt the county sold for the facility, a county official said Tuesday.

Norman Jesse, the county's manager of development, said Prairie Meadows Race Track has given the county $89 million -- enough to pay off outstanding general obligation and revenue bonds and operating loans from the county.

The $26.5 million of gaming revenue bonds the county sold last year to finance slot machines at Prairie Meadows would be legally defeased with the funds, Jesse said. Those bonds are set to mature in 1998.

The county also sold $38.8 million of tax-exempt GO bonds in 1993 to redeem industrial development bonds that were sold in 1984 to finance the race track and were remarketed three years later under a lease-purchase agreement.
Jesse said those bonds mature beginning in 2007 and ending in 2014. He said the race track's money would be placed with a trustee to pay off the bonds as they mature.
None of the bonds have early call dates, he added.
Meanwhile, the Polk County board is expected to approve getting an appraisal of Prairie Meadows's market value at the county board meeting Thursday, Jesse said.
In addition, the county may hire a consultant to conduct economic analyses of proposals for the race track, he said.

In September, Circus Circus Enterprises Inc., a Las Vegas-based gambling company, proposed buying Prairie Meadows from the county. Jesse said that proposal has since been withdrawn by the company, but that others are expected.
In the meantime, the county is still awaiting a private letter ruling from the Internal Revenue Service on whether the race track could be sold given the fact it was financed with tax-exempt bonds.
Jesse said bond counsel has advised the county to wait for the ruling before deciding to sell the track.
Prairie Meadows, which once faced bankruptcy, has been generating net profits of $4 million to $5 million a month as a result of the addition of slot machines last year, according to Jesse.
